       The three tags below fire real, billable hits wherever the page is
       served, which meant `npm run preview` and the GitHub Pages mirror were
       sending pageviews, Meta signals with domain=localhost, and Google Ads
       audience pings into the live properties — inflating the numbers with
       traffic that is us. It also keeps the browser's loading indicator
       spinning long after the content has painted, because these requests are
       still in flight, which reads as "the page never finishes loading".
       Only the production hostnames count. Everything else gets no tags at
       all, so local previews are silent and fast.
       WHEN they run is decided here too. Measured on the live site: Meta Pixel
       and Bing UET cost 13 Lighthouse points and 816ms of main-thread blocking
       — more than every Google tag combined — because ~214 KB of script parses
       and executes while the visitor is trying to read and tap.
       So they now wait for the first interaction instead of firing during
       load. The obvious objection to deferring is losing the visitor who never
       interacts, which is why there is also a fallback timer: anyone still on
       the page after it elapses is counted anyway. The only visitor missed is
       one who leaves within that window without scrolling, tapping or typing —
       already a bounce by any measure. A `scroll` counts, so on a page this
       tall almost everyone qualifies within a second or two. --><script></script><!-- No Google tag here on purpose.
       Cloudflare Zaraz already loads gtag.js for THE SAME GA4 property,
       G-DZXM0PNSJW, plus Google Ads AW-875530923, injected at the edge and so
       invisible in this file. Verified by loading the live page with this
       page's own snippets disabled: gtag.js still fetched three times and the
       Ads pixels still fired.
       Keeping a second copy here bought nothing and cost twice: every visit
       was counted twice in GA4, and the browser downloaded ~186 KB of gtag.js
       it already had. Removing it does not stop Google tracking — Zaraz does
       that now — but note the dependency has moved: if Zaraz is ever turned
       off in the Cloudflare dashboard, Analytics and Ads stop with it and this
       snippet has to come back.
       Meta and Bing below are NOT in Zaraz, so they stay. --><!-- End Google tag (handled by Zaraz) --><!-- Meta Pixel Code (deferred) --><script></script><!-- End Meta Pixel Code --><!-- Microsoft UET Tag (deferred) --><script></script><!-- End Microsoft UET Tag --><!-- Site-wide scroll reveal: reveals content blocks as they scroll into view.

       on paint timing; content stays visible if JS doesn't run.
       Adding `reveal-ready` hides EVERY content block until something adds
       `reveal-in`, so any failure between those two steps leaves the page
       permanently blank. That is a bad trade for an animation, so every path
       out of here un-hides: a throw removes the class, and a watchdog removes
       it if the reveal pass never completes for any reason at all. --><script></script><link rel="stylesheet" href="/_astro/index.C2bMx_Mh.css"><link rel="stylesheet" Experiences</a></div></section><section class="section faq-section" id="home-faq" data-astro-cid-lcdefpme><div class="section-heading" data-astro-cid-lcdefpme><p class="eyebrow" data-astro-cid-lcdefpme>FAQ</p><h2 data-astro-cid-lcdefpme>Common questions</h2></div><div class="faq-list" data-astro-cid-lcdefpme><details class="faq-item" open data-astro-cid-lcdefpme><summary data-astro-cid-lcdefpme>Can I learn to kitesurf in Sri Lanka as a complete beginner?</summary><p data-astro-cid-lcdefpme>Yes, Kalpitiya Lagoon is one of the better beginner spots in Sri Lanka because of the flat water and seasonal wind. Beginners can start with structured lessons and return to lagoon-side resort settings after each session.</p></details><details class="faq-item" data-astro-cid-lcdefpme><summary data-astro-cid-lcdefpme>Is Valampuri good for couples if only one person kitesurfs?</summary><p data-astro-cid-lcdefpme>Yes. This is one of the best reasons to stay here. One person can learn or ride while the other enjoys the pool, seafood, lagoon, garden, nature, and slow resort atmosphere.</p></details><details class="faq-item" data-astro-cid-lcdefpme><summary data-astro-cid-lcdefpme>Where is Valampuri located?</summary><p data-astro-cid-lcdefpme>Valampuri is in Kalpitiya, Sri Lanka, beside the lagoon and close to the main kitesurfing areas.</p></details><details class="faq-item" data-astro-cid-lcdefpme><summary data-astro-cid-lcdefpme>How far is Valampuri from town, can I walk?</summary><p data-astro-cid-lcdefpme>Valampuri is only about 2 km from Kalpitiya town, close enough to walk. A supermarket, bank, pharmacy, local shops and restaurants, the fish market and the island-hopping boat yard are all a short stroll away, plus a jetty on the doorstep for boat trips. Most Kalpitiya resorts sit 5–7 km out, so guests there pay for a tuk-tuk each way.</p></details><details class="faq-item" data-astro-cid-lcdefpme><summary data-astro-cid-lcdefpme>When is the best time to learn kitesurfing in Sri Lanka?</summary><p data-astro-cid-lcdefpme>The main wind seasons are usually May - October and December - March. Summer is stronger, while winter can be a little gentler depending on conditions.</p></details></div></section><script type="application/ld+json">{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"FAQPage","mainEntity":[{"@type":"Question","name":"Can I learn to kitesurf in Sri Lanka as a complete beginner?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes, Kalpitiya Lagoon is one of the better beginner spots in Sri Lanka because of the flat water and seasonal wind.
